title: A sharp bound on spacetime distance from quantum entanglement
authors: Zhi-Wei Wang, Arshid Shabir, Mir Faizal, Samuel L. Braunstein
abstract: Ryu-Takayanagi established how boundary entanglement encodes bulk area. We provide the metric counterpart: boundary mutual information imposes a rigorous lower bound on bulk geodesic separation that diverges logarithmically as correlations vanish. A multiscale iteration promotes this local inequality to a global obstruction to bulk connectivity. For parallel strips in AdS$_5$/CFT$_4$, the bound necessitates a quantum resolution of the classical mutual-information transition and fixes the asymptotic growth of geodesic distance.
summary: This work provides a quantitative link between quantum entanglement and spacetime geometry by deriving a 'metric-from-information' lower bound. It shows that the amount of boundary mutual information dictates how far apart points can be in the bulk spacetime, offering a powerful diagnostic tool beyond classical area laws.
main_problem: To establish a quantitative, metric counterpart showing how boundary mutual information constrains the bulk geodesic separation distance within holographic spacetime settings.
main_result: The paper derives a rigorous lower bound (Metric-from-information bound) stating that vanishing mutual information forces the allowed bulk geodesic separation to diverge logarithmically.
method: It combines quantum information measures, specifically Mutual Information $I(A:B)$, with holographic dictionary relations linking two-point functions to renormalized geodesic lengths $	ext{L}_{	ext{ren}}(x, y)$.
model_or_system: The analysis is set in the context of AdS/CFT correspondence and involves calculating bounds for a boundary manifold $\Sigma$ with disjoint regions $A$ and $B$. Specific applications include parallel strips in AdS$_5$/CFT$_4$.
key_observables: Boundary Mutual Information ($I(A:B)$) and renormalized Bulk Geodesic Distance ($	ext{L}_{	ext{ren}}(x, y)$).
important_parameters: The bound depends on calibration constants $\kappa_\Delta$ and $\epsilon_\star$, and the analysis distinguishes between semiclassical regimes.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on operating within a semiclassical holographic code subspace and assumes controlled truncation errors ($\epsilon_{	ext{code}} \ll 1$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates how short geodesics are permitted when $I(A:B)$ is large, while long geodesics are forced when $I(A:B)$ is small.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing a pairwise metric-from-information bound (Theorem 1) to extending this local inequality to global connectivity via a multiscale iteration (Theorem 2).
why_interesting: While focused on gravity/QFT, the core methodology—using entanglement measures like mutual information to constrain geometric properties—is highly relevant for understanding quantum correlations in open quantum systems.
